q: In which year did Swat join Pakistan?
facts: The princely state of Swat was merged into Pakistan in 1969.
note: Swat acceded Nov 1947 but fully merged in 1969; ambiguous. Fix: "In which year was Swat fully merged into Pakistan?" answer 1969 (D).

q: Who is the Governor of Sindh? (current affairs)
facts: Tessori was appointed Governor of Sindh in 2023. Verify latest.
note: Governor of Sindh is Nehal Hashmi since 13 Mar 2026 (thenews.pk, Wikipedia), replacing Tessori. Fix: replace option A with Nehal Hashmi, answer A.

q: Rearrange RAPISS to form the name of a city.
facts: RAPISS → PARIS (the capital of France).
note: RAPISS has 6 letters, Paris only 5. Fix question to "Rearrange PRAIS/APRIS to form the name of a city" (5 letters); answer D Paris.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q5) If 12 is divided by 3, what will be the half of the remainder (taking the result of the division as intended by the paper)?
facts: 12 divided by 3 gives 4, and half of 4 is 2 (this is the answer given in the paper key).
rel: Tip: strictly, 12 divided by 3 leaves remainder 0, but such papers use the word remainder for the result of the division.
note: Wording is awkward/wrong (remainder of 12/3 is 0). Rewrite question: "If 12 is divided by 3, what is half of the result?" Options A 4, B 1, C 0, D 2; answer D.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q18) Which letter comes next: B, D, G, L, ?
facts: Positions are 2, 4, 7, 12 with differences 2, 3, 5, and each difference is one more than a power of 2 (2^0+1, 2^1+1 and so on: 2, 3, 5, 9). Next difference is 9: 12 + 9 = 21, which is U. Another reading of the gaps (2, 3, 5, 8) would give T, but the paper's answer key is U.
rel: Tip: if differences are not simple, subtract a constant from them and look for powers of 2.
note: Differences 2,3,5,7 are consecutive primes, so next is 12+7 = 19 = S (the classic B,D,G,L,S series). The "2^n+1" reading and the Fibonacci reading (T) are weaker and conflict; answer S is option B.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q21) Which letter comes next: B, D, G, L, ?
facts: Positions are 2, 4, 7, 12 with differences 2, 3, 5. Each difference is one more than a power of 2 (2, 3, 5, 9), so next is +9: 12 + 9 = 21, which is U. Another reading of the gaps (2, 3, 5, 8) would give T, but the paper's answer key is U.
rel: Tip: if differences are not simple, subtract a constant from them and look for powers of 2.
note: Same series as 1731: prime gaps 2,3,5,7 give 12+7 = 19 = S (option B). Update reason text accordingly.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q3) Which one of the following is different? A. PQO, B. KJL, C. UYW, D. SRT, E. FEG
facts: KJL, SRT and FEG each go one step back then two steps forward (-1, +2). PQO goes forward then back (+1, -2), the reverse of that pattern, which is the answer given in the key.
rel: Tip: write the step sizes between neighbouring letters, as in +1, -2, to spot the odd group.
note: UYW is +4,-2 so it also breaks the (-1,+2) pattern; PQO (+1,-2) is the intended odd one. Fix option C: replace UYW with UTV (-1,+2). Options A PQO, B KJL, C UTV, D SRT, E FEG; answer A.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q19) What number comes next in the series: 8, 5, 3, 2, ?
facts: The differences are 3, 2, 1, so the next difference is 1 (the gaps themselves shrink by 1). 2 - 1 = 1.
rel: Tip: when the differences form their own pattern, extend the pattern of differences.
note: Series 8,5,3,2 fits both reverse Fibonacci (next 1) and differences 3,2,1,0 (next 2); the stated reason is also faulty. Change series to 13, 8, 5, 3, 2, ? with options 0, 1, 2, -1; answer B (1). Differences 5,3,2,1 are no longer a simple pattern, so only reverse Fibonacci fits.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 25) On what date was the Objective Resolution passed (the chart gives 7 March)?
facts: The Constituent Assembly passed it on 12 March 1949.
rel: The chart says 7 March, which is not the accepted date; it was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan.
note: Remove the confusing "(the chart gives 7 March)". Objective Resolution was moved 7 March and passed 12 March 1949. Question: "On what date was the Objective Resolution passed by the Constituent Assembly?" Options unchanged; answer B.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 31) What were the years of the first war between Pakistan and India (chart says 1947 to 1949)?
facts: The war began in October 1947 and the UN-brokered ceasefire took effect on 1 January 1949; it is usually called the 1947-48 war.
rel: Many books call it the 1947-48 war.
note: Option A "1947-49 (to 1950)" is garbled and 1947-49 is arguable (ceasefire 1 Jan 1949). Question: "In which years was the first Indo-Pak war fought?" Options A 1948-49, B 1950-51, C 1949-50, D 1947-48; answer D.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 22) How many seats did the Awami League win in the National Assembly election of 1970?
facts: The Awami League of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman won 160 general seats, all but two of East Pakistan's seats.
rel: Counting reserved women seats, its tally rose to 167 of 313 seats.
note: 160 is general seats only (167 with reserved women seats). Question: "How many general seats did the Awami League win in the 1970 National Assembly election?" Options unchanged; answer C (160).

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 91) In which year was the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (Aligarh) College established?
facts: The school was begun in 1875 and upgraded to MAO College in 1877 by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
rel: The college became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
note: MAO school began 1875, college status 1877. Question: "In which year was the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental School upgraded to MAO College?" Options unchanged; answer C (1877).

q: Who was the first Chief Justice of Pakistan?
facts: Sir Abdul Rashid became the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court of Pakistan in 1949.
rel: Muhammad Munir succeeded him as Chief Justice in 1954.
note: B and C are the same person (Sir Abdul Rashid, first Chief Justice, 1949-54). Change option C to "Muhammad Shahabuddin"; options A Muhammad Munir, B Sir Abdul Rashid, C Muhammad Shahabuddin, D Sheikh Abdur Rahman; answer B.

q: Rearrange the letters PEOLARD to form a correct English word.
facts: The letters P, E, O, L, A, R, D rearrange to make LEOPARD, a big cat.
rel: The leopard is a big cat found in Africa and Asia, and it is a strong climber.
note: PEOLARD also forms PAROLED (option C), same letters. Replace C with a non-anagram such as "Parole". Options: A. Leopard B. Pearl C. Parole D. Prelude; answer A.

q: In which year was CENTO (Central Treaty Organization, formerly the Baghdad Pact) established?
facts: The Baghdad Pact was signed in 1955 and was renamed CENTO in 1959 after Iraq withdrew.
rel: Pakistan was a member of both CENTO and SEATO.
note: Ambiguous: Baghdad Pact 1955, name CENTO from 1959. Reword to "In which year was the Baghdad Pact signed?" keep options, answer B (1955).

q: What is the motto given by the Quaid-e-Azam to the nation?
facts: The Quaid-e-Azam gave the nation the motto Unity, Faith, Discipline (Ittehad, Yaqeen-e-Muhkam, Nazm). This is the order used in his speeches and in Pakistani textbooks.
rel: In Urdu the motto is often written as Ittehad, Tanzeem, Yaqeen-e-Muhkam; some books change the order, but Unity, Faith, Discipline is the standard English form.
note: A and B are the same words in different order; the official national motto is Faith, Unity, Discipline while Quaid's phrase is often given as Unity, Faith, Discipline. Replace B with a distinct wrong option (e.g. "Peace, Progress, Prosperity") and keep A as answer, or ask "Which three words make up the motto".

q: To which language group does the Sindhi language belong, among the given options?
facts: Sindhi is an Indo-Aryan language that developed from Sanskrit and Prakrit. Of the given options, Sanskrit is the ancestral language group.
rel: Sindhi is the official language of Sindh province and is written in a Perso-Arabic script.
note: Persian is Iranian, Urdu/Hindi are not parents; "language group" wording is loose. Rewrite: "Sindhi belongs to which language family? A. Indo-Aryan B. Dravidian C. Iranian D. Semitic", answer A.

q: Rearrange the letters V I S R E L to make a word. What is the second last letter of that word?
facts: The letters form the word SILVER. Its letters are S, I, L, V, E, R so the second last letter is E.
rel: Silver has the chemical symbol Ag from the Latin argentum.
note: VISREL gives SILVER, SLIVER, LIVERS (second-last E or R), ambiguous. Replace letters with E T W A R (WATER, unique); options A. E B. T C. R D. A; answer A (E).

q: Vehicle is to tyres as sound is to ___ ?
facts: A vehicle has tyres as a part, and sound is made up of or travels as waves. The analogy links a thing with its essential component.
rel: Sound waves are longitudinal mechanical waves that need a medium.
note: Weak analogy (tyres are a part of a vehicle, waves are not a part of sound). Replace with a clear one, e.g. "Vehicle is to road as ship is to ___": Sea (answer), with other options Sky, Silence, Speed.

q: Which is the longest river flowing within India?
facts: The Ganga is the longest river flowing mainly within India, about 2,500 km.
rel: The Indus and Brahmaputra are longer overall but rise outside India.
note: Ambiguous: Ganga is longest river of India (2,525 km) but flows into Bangladesh; Godavari is longest wholly within India. Rewrite as "Which is the longest river of India?" keep A Ganga, or "longest river flowing entirely within India?" answer C Godavari. Prefer first: keep A, change question wording to "longest river of India".

q: Complete the sentence: Our team ______ their track suits.
facts: "Team" is treated here as one unit, so the singular verb "is wearing" is used.
rel: In British English a collective noun like team can also take a plural verb, but the singular is the textbook answer.
note: "their track suits" requires plural verb; "are wearing" agrees with the plural pronoun (collective noun treated as plural). Marked "is wearing" mismatches "their".

q: Car is to wheel as sound is to what?
facts: A car moves by its wheels in the same way that sound travels as waves.
rel: Sound is a mechanical wave and cannot travel through a vacuum.
note: Analogy is flawed (wheel is a part of car; wave is not a part of sound). Rewrite: "Car is to wheel as clock is to ?" A. Hands B. Time C. Wall D. Watch, answer A.

q: Aliza is 3 times as old as Asad. When Asad was 6, Aliza was 3 times his age. How old will Aliza be when Asad is 14?
facts: When Asad was 6, Aliza was 3 x 6 = 18. The gap is 18 - 6 = 12 years, which never changes. When Asad is 14, Aliza is 14 + 12 = 26.
rel: The age gap between two people stays the same all their lives.
note: Question is self-contradictory (cannot be 3x as old now and at 6). Fix: "Aliza is 12 years older than Asad. When Asad was 6, Aliza was 3 times his age (18). How old will Aliza be when Asad is 14?" Options unchanged, answer C (26 years). Alternative: remove "now" sentence.

q: Vehicle is to wheels as sound is to what?
facts: A vehicle moves on wheels, and sound travels as waves.
rel: Analogy questions: find the relationship in the first pair and apply it to the second.
note: Analogy is weak (wheels are a part of a vehicle; waves are not a part of sound). Rewrite e.g. "Vehicle is to road as sound is to ?" or replace with a clear analogy; as is, A is only a loose fit

q: After arranging the letters of RAPISS, it becomes the name of a country, city, ocean or state. Which one is it?
facts: The word is a scrambled PARIS (the extra S in the source spelling is a typo), the capital city of France. So it is a city.
rel: Anagram questions: look for a familiar name first, then check that every letter is used.
note: RAPISS has an extra S and cannot make PARIS. Fix question to "PARIS"/"After arranging the letters of SIRAP (or PARIS scrambled as RAPIS)..." with letters exactly matching; answer A City stays
